memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: So Eleazar the priest collected the bronze censers brought by those who had been burned up, and he had them hammered out to overlay the altar, as the Lord directed through Moses. This was to remind the Israelites that no one except a descendant of Aaron should come to burn incense before the Lord, or he would become like Korah and his followers. — Num 16:39-40 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The bronze censers become a permanent covering on the altar — a memorial hammered into the very place of worship. Every time the Israelites came to the altar, they would see it and remember: God is holy, and He must be approached the way He has appointed. The warning was not meant to terrify them away from God, but to teach them to draw near rightly.

God knows how quickly we forget. He had just displayed His holiness in unmistakable ways, yet He provided a lasting, visible reminder so the lesson would not fade with time. We are prone to let hard truths slip from memory once the immediate moment passes. God graciously builds reminders into our lives so that we keep walking in reverence and truth.

There is something significant in where the reminder was placed: on the altar, the place of sacrifice and worship. The lesson about God's holiness was woven right into the heart of their approach to Him. Reverence and worship belong together. We cannot truly worship a God we do not revere, nor rightly revere a God we refuse to worship.

For us, the altar points forward to the cross, where the perfect and final sacrifice was offered. There, God's holiness and His mercy meet. We come to worship not with bronze censers but through the finished work of Christ. And rather than a memorial of judgment warning us to keep our distance, we have the memorial He gave us — the bread and the cup — reminding us that the way to God stands open through His body and blood. What was once a warning to keep away has become, in Christ, an invitation to come near.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What reminders help you keep walking in reverence before God?
2. Why do reverence and worship belong together?
3. How does the cross transform a warning to keep away into an invitation to come near?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for building reminders into my life that keep me walking in reverence and truth. Thank You that the way to You now stands open through the sacrifice of Christ. Draw me near to worship You with awe and with love. Amen.
